# 1 Chronicles Chapter 25 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 383r–383v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_025_page_001.jpg, 1CH_025_page_002.jpg

---

**25:1** And-set-apart [vayyavdel] David and-the-commanders of-the-host [sarey ha-tsava] for-the-service the-sons of-Asaf and-Heyman and-Yedutun, the-ones-prophesying [ha-nib'im] with-lyres [be-khinnorot] and-with-harps [u-vinvalim] and-with-cymbals [u-vimtsiltayim]. And-was the-number of-the-men of-the-work [anshey ha-melakhah] for-their-service:

**25:2** To-the-sons of-Asaf: Zakkur, and-Yosef, and-Netanyah, and-Asar'elah — sons of-Asaf, upon the-hand of-Asaf, the-one-prophesying [ha-niba] upon the-hands of-the-king.

**25:3** To-Yedutun — the-sons of-Yedutun: Gedalyahu, and-Tseri, and-Yeshayahu, Chashabvyahu and-Mattityahu — six, upon the-hands of-their-father Yedutun, with-the-lyre [ba-kinnor], the-one-prophesying [ha-niba] for-giving-thanks [al-hodot] and-for-praising [u-le-hallel] YHWH.

**25:4** To-Heyman — the-sons of-Heyman: Buqqiyyahu, Mattanyahu, Uzzi'el, Shevu'el, and-Yerimot, Chananyah, Chanani, Eli'atah, Giddalti, and-Romamti-Ezer, Yoshbeqashah, Malloti, Hotir, Machazi'ot. **25:5** All these [were] sons of-Heyman, the-seer of-the-king [chozeh ha-melekh] in-the-words of-God [be-divrey ha-elohim], to-lift-up [le-harim] a-horn [qeren]. And-gave God to-Heyman fourteen sons and-three daughters.

**25:6** All these [were] upon the-hands of-their-father in-the-song [ba-shir] of-the-house of-YHWH, with-cymbals, harps, and-lyres, for-the-service of-the-house of-God [ha-elohim], upon the-hands of-the-king — Asaf, and-Yedutun, and-Heyman.

**25:7** And-was their-number with their-brothers, the-ones-trained [ha-melummadim] in-song to-YHWH, all the-skillful-ones [kol ha-mevin] — two-hundred and-eighty-eight.

**25:8** And-they-cast lots [vayyappilu goralot], watch [mishmeret] corresponding to [le-ummat] watch, the-small as the-great, the-skillful [mevin] with the-learner [talmid].

**25:9** And-came-out the-lot, the-first, for-Asaf — to-Yosef; the-second — Gedalyahu, he and-his-brothers and-his-sons — twelve; **25:10** the-third — Zakkur, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:11** the-fourth — to-Yitsri, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:12** the-fifth — Netanyahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:13** the-sixth — Buqqiyyahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:14** the-seventh — Yesar'elah, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:15** the-eighth — Yeshayahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:16** the-ninth — Mattanyahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:17** the-tenth — Shim'i, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:18** the-eleventh — Azar'el, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:19** the-twelfth — to-Chashabvyah, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:20** the-thirteenth — Shuva'el, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:21** the-fourteenth — Mattityahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:22** the-fifteenth — to-Yeremot, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:23** the-sixteenth — to-Chananyahu, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:24** the-seventeenth — to-Yoshbeqashah, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:25** the-eighteenth — to-Chanani, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:26** the-nineteenth — to-Malloti, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:27** the-twentieth — to-Eli'atah, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:28** the-twenty-first — to-Hotir, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:29** the-twenty-second — to-Giddalti, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:30** the-twenty-third — to-Machazi'ot, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve; **25:31** the-twenty-fourth — to-Romamti-Ezer, his-sons and-his-brothers — twelve.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — ha-nib'im (the-ones-prophesying):** The Chronicler uses the niphal participle of *naba* (to prophesy) to describe musical performance. This is extraordinary — music is prophecy. The verb is the same used for Saul among the prophets (1 Sam 10:10) and for prophetic ecstasy. The Chronicler has theologized the role of the temple musician.

**v.4 — Heman's sons' names:** The last nine names of Heman's sons (from Hannaniah onward) have been read by some scholars as a liturgical prayer fragment: "Be gracious to me, O God / Be gracious to me / You are my God / I have magnified and exalted / He who sits in need / I have given abundant visions." This is debated but linguistically plausible.

**v.5 — chozeh ha-melekh (seer of-the-king):** Heman bears the title *chozeh* — seer/visionary — elevating the chief musician to prophetic status. "To lift up a horn" (*le-harim qeren*) means to exalt power or praise.

**v.8 — mevin with talmid:** "The skillful with the learner" — an early use of *talmid* (student/disciple), showing that musical training was formal, with masters and apprentices.

*— EMET*
